title: The hospitality that brought fear
intro: In a city consumed by wickedness, a faithful servant received unexpected visitors one day. Concerned for their safety, this individual offered protection, but the city's people demanded something shameful. Warned of an impending doom, the servant fled with family under cover of darkness, leaving behind a city marked for destruction. Who is this lone believer?
clues: I was sent as a messenger to a people who had engaged in shameful acts.
Unexpected visitors came to my home, and I was more worried for their safety than my own.
My people demanded to see my guests for wicked intentions, and I tried to reason with them.
My visitors revealed themselves as angels and commanded me to take my family and leave in the night.
My wife did not heed the call to escape and faced the same destruction as my people.
My city was overturned with a rain of stones of layered clay, its highest parts brought lowest.

identity.label: Who Am I?
options: Prophet Lut
Prophet Musa
Prophet Ibrahim
Prophet Nuh
Prophet Hud

trial.label: Trial/Event
options: The demand of my people to approach my guests wickedly
The parting of the sea to escape a tyrant
The building of a great ark amid mockery
The sacrifice of my son in a test of faith
The experience of being swallowed by a great fish
trial.answer: The demand of my people to approach my guests wickedly

location.label: Key Element
options: The overturned city of my people
The mountain where I received divine speech
The ark that sailed through a great flood
The she-camel that emerged from the rock
The garden with a hidden righteous visitor
location.answer: The overturned city of my people

outcome.label: Outcome
options: I was saved with my family before my city was overturned
I led my people to freedom across the sea
I built a great ark and survived a mighty flood
I was given dominion over the winds and jinn
I patiently endured suffering and was rewarded with family
outcome.answer: I was saved with my family before my city was overturned

arabic: قَالَ لَوْ أَنَّ لِى بِكُمْ قُوَّةً أَوْ ءَاوِىٓ إِلَىٰ رُكْنٍۢ شَدِيدٍۢ
verse: He said, "If only I had against you some power or could take refuge in a strong support." (11:80)
